assumptions: FREE divergence (Hawkins et al., PNAS 2018) as freebarcodes computes it.
limits: Exhaustive over 4^k, so long codes are slow; GC and homopolymer filters prune after generation.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which barcodes of this length correct this many insertions, deletions and substitutions?

description: Generate INDEL-correcting barcodes — FREE divergence codes (Hawkins et al., PNAS 2018) — by reserving each codeword's error sphere over the whole 4^k space, so the guarantee survives an insertion or deletion rather than only a substitution. Or prune a set you already own down to a valid FREE code, and see which members' decode spheres collided. This is a different construction from design_barcodes' distance-based search, and answers a different question: a Levenshtein-distance set corrects indels between two barcodes, a FREE code corrects them in the read.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

barcodes.description: the set to prune — required when `mode` is `prune`, ignored when generating. Only applies when mode is prune.

length.description: barcode length k. The search is over the whole 4^k space, so cost rises steeply with it.

limit.description: stop after this many codewords. 0 = take the whole code. Advanced.

max_errors.description: how many insertions/deletions/substitutions each codeword must tolerate. Each extra error costs most of the code.

max_gc.description: reject a candidate above this GC fraction. 0 = no limit. Advanced.

max_homopolymer.description: reject a candidate with a run of this many identical bases. 0 = no limit. Advanced.

mode.description: generate a new code, or prune an existing set down to a valid one. Values: generate (Generate a code), prune (Prune a set to a valid code).

reserved.description: codewords already in use, whose decode spheres are claimed BEFORE generation — this is how a code is EXTENDED rather than regenerated, so what comes back is compatible with the indexes a lab already owns.

name: design_free_codes

barcodes.description: the codewords — generated, or the ones that survived pruning

dropped.description: prune only: the codewords removed because their decode spheres collided — a user pruning their own set needs to know which indexes to stop using, not how many
